q: Who writes the guides on this blog?
a: The same team that quotes, proofs and prints the orders. Each guide answers a question we get on the phone or in the quote form every week, and the advice reflects what has worked and failed on real jobs rather than supplier marketing.

q: How do I decide between matte and glossy from the guides?
a: The finish guide comes down to two rules: gloss where color depth matters and the sticker is seen in diffuse light, matte where there is text to read or glare from overhead lighting. Both cost the same, so the choice is about the artwork and the surface.

q: Do the lifespan figures in the outdoor guide apply to my climate?
a: They are ranges for laminated vinyl on vertical surfaces in typical US conditions. Desert sun and coastal salt shorten them; shaded northern sites extend them. Horizontal surfaces lose about a third because water and sun hit them harder.

q: Is the eco-friendly materials guide a sales page?
a: No. It explains what recyclable, biodegradable and compostable actually mean on a sticker, where each claim holds up and where it does not. Several readers end up choosing plain paper after reading it, which is the right outcome for many products.

q: Which guide should I read before my first order?
a: The sizing guide. Most first-order problems are stickers that are too small to read or too large for the surface. It includes reading-distance rules and a method for testing size with a paper print before you commit.

q: What is the difference between a sticker, a decal and a label?
a: The blog has a full guide, but in short: a sticker is any printed adhesive piece, a decal is a graphic applied once to a large surface such as a vehicle or window, and a label identifies a product and ships on rolls or sheets. The construction overlaps; the purpose and format differ.

q: Can I ask for a guide on a topic that is not covered?
a: Yes. Send the question through the contact page. If it comes up often enough we write it up, and in the meantime we answer it directly by email. Recent requests have covered dishwasher-safe labels and inside-glass window decals.

q: Do the guides cover how to apply stickers?
a: The outdoor guide covers surface preparation, temperature and wet application for large pieces, because application decides more of a sticker's life than the material. Shorter application notes also appear on each product page.

q: Are the guides updated when materials change?
a: Yes. Each article carries its publication date, and we revise figures when a film or laminate we use changes. If a guide and a quote ever disagree, the quote is current, because it is written for your exact job.

q: Can I share or reprint a guide?
a: Linking to a guide is always fine. Reprinting an article in full needs permission; email us with where it will appear. Short quotes with a link back are welcome, and we are happy to answer follow-up questions from your readers.
